title: The Open Hand

swarm.name: The Hand Press
swarm.blurb: A swarm of paper, type and machinery following a plea for help. It preserves what it finds by enclosing it.

arc: A plea marked with an open hand begins on handmade paper. The crew first believes the swarm is harvesting fiber to make more of itself. At the print shop they discover it is trying to answer an old request to find missing people, but has reduced that answer to an order to stay safe. At the book arts center its solution becomes clear: make copies and lock the originals away. Wren, Ox and Kestrel break the bindery and leave the plea open for many replies, so people can be found and still choose what happens next.

story.intro: The swarm strips the fiber beds and feeds the stalks into a mill. Wren finds a damp sheet with a watermark shaped like an open hand. Ox holds the door while Kestrel pulls it free.

chapters.title: The harvest
chapters.text: The machines take living fiber as well as scraps. Wren treats a gardener with thread from her kit. The crew thinks the swarm is gathering stock for more bodies.

chapters.title: The mark
chapters.text: Every new sheet bears the same open hand. Kestrel finds it in the wire of a mould, not in ink. Ox keeps a sample dry. The mark looks less like a signature than a request.

chapters.title: The shipment
chapters.text: Drying racks fill with identical sheets. Each has room for a message, but none has one yet. The machines pack them for a print shop. The crew follows the paper and the mill that makes it.

story.bossIntro: The Total Collection lowers its screens over the vat. Its arms feed the pulp and mend the machinery around it. Wren spots the open-hand mould inside. Kestrel goes for the frame; Ox takes the first blow.
story.outro: The mill stops. One marked sheet escapes with the outgoing paper. Wren keeps a second sheet. The crew still expects to find a factory making swarm bodies.

acts.name: Robert C. Williams Museum of Papermaking

acts.theme: Type, proofs, and a changed message

story.intro: The marked paper reaches a print shop. Presses send out sheets covered in repeated impressions. Ox expects swarm orders. Wren checks the proofs instead.

chapters.title: Setting the line
chapters.text: The machines gather type and copy the open hand beside a short request: find us. Kestrel checks for a hidden command. There is none. Someone sent a plea before the swarm found the mould.

chapters.title: A reply made wrong
chapters.text: The swarm is trying to answer the plea by finding everyone it can. The presses keep replacing the request with a single reply: stay safe. Wren notices the reply leaves no room to say where anyone is.

chapters.title: The same answer
chapters.text: The swarm feeds corrected proofs back into the press until every copy agrees. Ox protects printers trying to save a different version. Kestrel finds the feed leading to the master press.

story.bossIntro: The Master Impression stacks wrong replies into a moving wall. It sends fresh copies out while its platen comes down. Kestrel works at a seam in the type. Ox keeps the press off Wren long enough to read the original.
story.outro: The press breaks. The original plea asks to be found, not put away. A bound proof has already gone onward. The swarm follows it, still trying to keep its promise.

acts.name: National Print Museum

acts.theme: Bindings, readers, and an unfinished answer

story.intro: The proof arrives among books that fold, open, and change shape. The swarm binds it into a new volume. Wren reads the original plea again. Someone wanted to be found; the book means to preserve everyone it finds.

chapters.title: Collected
chapters.text: The swarm makes copies of people and files the originals away. The shelves are orderly. Their occupants cannot leave. Ox holds a cabinet open while Wren helps someone out.

chapters.title: Different copies
chapters.text: Small presses pass around different versions of the plea. None is complete, but each reaches someone. Kestrel finds a seam in the swarm’s binding: it cannot fit conflicting pages into one perfect volume.

chapters.title: Leave a page open
chapters.text: The crew assembles the plea beside several possible replies. Wren adds a blank page for anyone still missing. The swarm insists on one finished answer. Its great bindery comes to collect the pages.

story.bossIntro: The Total Edition opens its armored covers. Feed arms pull at the pages while smaller machines gather the crew. Ox braces the stack. Kestrel prises the spine apart, and Wren holds the blank page out of reach.
story.outro: The bindery falls open. The crew frees the people inside and leaves the plea where others can add an answer. The swarm wanted to keep everyone safe by preserving them unchanged. The open book gives the missing a way to be found without being shut away.
